tg_gain_pct: tg128 +0.59% / +0.53% / +1.20% / +1.25% (dense, dense, MoE, Q4_0) on the idle machine -- none clears disjoint AND >=1%
notes: Own idea from the cross-backend sweep: Vulkan uses hardware subgroupAdd and CUDA >=Ampere uses __reduce_add_sync, but AMD falls through to a shfl_xor loop (5 rounds; gfx1201 reports warpSize=32, so wave32 not wave64 -- an earlier note saying 6 rounds on wave64 was wrong). Implemented with ds_swizzle + permlanex16 + permlane64, gated to gfx1100/1101/1102/1200/1201. Patch: patches/dpp_warp_reduce.diff. Run1 tg128 +1.09/+0.92/+1.29%; Run2 +1.01/+1.07/+4.93%. The +4.93% is inflated by a noisy OLMoE baseline ([219.60..245.86]); the patched side is stable across both runs ([247.29..249.31] and [247.91..249.26]), so the true MoE figure is ~+1.3% vs the clean baseline [245.24..245.71]. NOTE: an initial run was recorded as REJECTED (-6.82% MoE) -- that was GPU contention from Chrome/Parsec, not the kernel; the tell was a 15% spread on the patched side against 0.3% on the baseline. Small but uniform and free. RECLASSIFIED 2026-09-08 VALIDATED -> NEGLIGIBLE. Re-measured on the idle machine (chrome=0), 5 reps, vs frozen base: Qwen3-4B-Q4_K_M +0.59%, Qwen3-8B-Q4_K_M +0.53% (both disjoint ranges but under the 1% effect-size floor), OLMoE +1.20% and Q4_0 +1.25% (both overlapping ranges). Every cell is positive and correctness still passes (0 failing ops), but nothing satisfies our rule of disjoint ranges AND >=1% effect -- the same rule that demoted #27962 and #28178. The earlier +1.0/+1.3% VALIDATED verdict came from sessions with Parsec/Chrome/WebView active, which inflated the apparent effect by depressing the baseline. Not a v2 candidate on current evidence: ~0.5-1.2% for 42 lines of AMD-specific DPP intrinsics gated to five gfx targets. Kept in the database as a measured near-miss, not deleted. PROMOTED TO v2-candidate 2026-09-08 by explicit user decision, despite the NEGLIGIBLE status. Rationale on record: uniformly positive (+0.5-1.2% decode across 4 models), never negative on any cell, 0 failing ops. Status stays NEGLIGIBLE because it does not clear our disjoint-AND->=1% rule; the release field records the shipping decision, not the measurement verdict. MUST BE RE-MEASURED ON TOP OF #23685 before it is merged into a v2 stack: #23685 restructures lanes_per_block and the per-lane quant indexing that feed warp_reduce_sum, which is exactly what this patch replaces, so a sub-1% margin measured against the frozen base may not survive on top of it. They apply together cleanly (verified), but co-applying is not co-benefiting. REJECTED AND REMOVED FROM v2 2026-09-08. With the corrected correctness check (exit code + backend verdict, not just per-op ': FAIL' lines) DPP fails deterministically: 3 of 3 runs on the same binary give exit 1 with GATED_DELTA_NET, MUL_MAT_VEC_FUSION and TOPK_MOE failing, and the passing-op count collapses from ~14697 to ~12480, i.e. roughly 2200 cases lost. This is exactly the failure that broke the assembled v2 stack. The earlier '0 failing ops, twice' verdicts were produced by the broken parser and were wrong. Combined with its measured gain of only +0.5..1.2% -- at or below the ~0.95% noise floor -- there is no case for shipping it. The underlying observation still stands (AMD has no hardware reduction path where NVIDIA does); this particular implementation is not correct on our backend.

title: own experiment: tune the RDNA4 ne11 threshold in ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvf (float matvec)
tg_gain_pct: none - current ne11<=8 is OPTIMAL for RDNA4; every lower threshold regresses 10-23% on both MoE models
gate: n/a - swept and rejected; control flat within +/-1.6%
notes: From the second cross-backend sweep. Gap is real: fp32_mma_hardware_available() admits CDNA only, so in ggml_cuda_should_use_mmvf the AMD F32 branch gives CDNA a measured 'ne11 <= 3' while RDNA4 falls to a blanket 'ne11 <= 8' that nobody tuned. INSTRUMENTED the mmvf dispatch branch in ggml_cuda_mul_mat and counted real calls: Qwen3-4B with -fa 1 = 0 hits; OLMoE with -fa 1 = 34 hits (all f32, ne01=64, the MoE router matmul); Qwen3-4B with -fa 0 = 144 hits (f16, ne01=256/128, the attention matmuls FA would otherwise absorb); OLMoE with -fa 0 = 98 hits. SO THE PATH IS LIVE -- an earlier claim that our quantized models never take it was wrong. It is nevertheless dead as a tuning target because max_ne11 == 1 in ALL FOUR runs: 1 satisfies both '<=3' and '<=8', so no value of the threshold alters dispatch on this workload. Would only matter for batched decode (ne11 2..8), the same blind spot as the MMVQ crossover candidate. INCIDENTAL: disabling flash attention costs Qwen3-4B -7.8% tg128 (126.82->116.89) and -22.9% pp512 (6007->4633), confirming our default benchmarks run with FA active. RE-OPENED AND TESTED 2026-09-08 once llama-batched-bench existed. Corrected scope first: F16 is ALREADY tuned for RDNA4 (should_use_mmvf line 844: RDNA4 -> ne11<=5), so the only untuned AMD path is F32, whose sole occurrence on our workload is the MoE router matmul f32[2048,64]. SWEPT T in {1,2,3,4} vs base(8) with batched-bench at npl 1,2,4,8 on OLMoE + gemma4-26B-A4B, with Qwen3-4B as a NULL CONTROL (probe showed zero mmvf calls there). RESULT: the current value is optimal and every reduction is a significant REGRESSION -- OLMoE B2 -19.9% at T=1, B4 -14.7..-16.1% at T=1..3, B8 -10.7..-11.8% at all T<8; gemma B4 -17.5..-17.7%, B8 -10.5..-11.2%. Control flat within +/-1.6% on every cell, and the damage always appears at exactly the ne11 value a given threshold newly excludes (T=4 leaves B4 at +0.4% but still breaks B8), so the pattern is coherent rather than noise. EXPLANATION: the gate is fp32_mma_hardware_available, which admits CDNA only. Architectures WITH fp32 matrix cores leave mmvf earlier because their alternative is better; RDNA4 has no fp32 MMA, so remaining on the float matvec kernel up to ne11=8 is correct. The permissive fallthrough is a correct consequence of the hardware, not an oversight. IMPORTANT METHODOLOGICAL NOTE: this falsifies the general inference "CDNA tuned + RDNA permissive => missed optimisation" that motivated this lead. RDNA4-MMVQ-XOVER rests on its own measurement, not on that pattern.

title: finding: build reproducibility broken, but no systematic perf offset; noise floor measured
tg_gain_pct: n/a - hypothesis NOT confirmed; build offset -0.56%..+0.32%, within a ~0.95% noise floor
notes: Observed while validating #28432 and #27044. Our A/B compares the STORED bin-baseline binaries against a FRESHLY COMPILED patched binary. In that batch every cell of both patches came out slightly negative (-0.17% to -1.51%), INCLUDING the dense control under #27044 -- a patch that only changes a buffer-size calculation on the MoE ids-path and cannot affect a dense model. That points to a systematic ~1% offset between cached and fresh builds rather than any patch effect. CONSEQUENCE: small positive effects are under-credited and small negatives exaggerated, in every A/B this project has run. Our disjoint-AND->=1% rule absorbs some of it but this is an unmeasured floor. FIX: run a NULL-PATCH CONTROL -- build the unmodified frozen base fresh and A/B it against bin-baseline; whatever difference appears is pure methodology and should be subtracted from, or at least reported alongside, sub-2% verdicts. NOT YET RUN. RESOLVED 2026-09-08 by a NULL-PATCH CONTROL: reverted to the frozen base with NO patch, rebuilt the identical source, and ran cached-vs-fresh-vs-cached (A/B/A) at 5 reps on 3 models. RESULT 1 -- MY HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG: the build offset (fresh vs the mean of both cached runs) spans -0.56% to +0.32% with mean ~0, i.e. NO directional bias, and it is SMALLER than the pure run-to-run noise measured between the two cached runs of the identical binary (-0.95% to +0.46%). The uniformly negative cells in the #28432/#27044 batch were ordinary session variance that happened to land one way; I over-read a pattern from six cells. All previously recorded verdicts stand. RESULT 2 -- A DIFFERENT REAL DEFECT: the binaries are NOT byte-reproducible. ggml-hip.dll cached 74,917,888 b vs fresh 74,918,912 b, llama.dll 3,307,520 b vs 3,309,568 b -- different SIZES, so genuine code differences, not timestamps. The project's stated invariant 'revert must reproduce the byte-identical upstream DLL' is therefore FALSE and cannot be used as a build-correctness check. Most likely cause: bin-baseline predates today's project consolidation and CMake cache regeneration. Practical impact is nil (the perf delta is within noise) but the invariant should be dropped from the method description or bin-baseline rebuilt. RESULT 3 -- CALIBRATION: the same-binary noise floor reaches ~0.95% on pp512, so our >=1% effect-size rule sits directly on top of the floor and is only safe because disjoint ranges are ALSO required. Anything reported between 1% and 2% is near the floor -- notably DPP-reduce at +0.5..1.2%.

title: CUDA: fix NORM/RMS_NORM/L2_NORM for more than 65535 channels or samples
tg_gain_pct: no speed change (pp512 -1.16%, tg128 -0.32%, within noise); +8 op cases now PASSING
gate: test-only probe: all 7 added cases pass on our shipped kernel
notes: Track B (capability, not speed). Acceptance: applies + builds + 0 failing ops + the OK count rises + no perf regression. METRIC NOTE: an earlier pass counted OK, FAIL and NOT SUPPORTED together and was discarded -- a patch can add test cases that report NOT SUPPORTED, which is the opposite of capability. Re-measured counting OK only, with NOT SUPPORTED tracked separately. Baseline on gfx1201: OK 14691, NOT SUPPORTED 7579, FAIL 0. The OK count carries +/-1 jitter between sessions, so +1 is not evidence. Lets NORM/RMS_NORM/L2_NORM handle >65535 channels or samples, which very large models need. 8 new cases, all passing, no ops moved into NOT SUPPORTED. || HAND-MERGE ATTEMPTED AND STOPPED 2026-09-10. This is not a merge conflict, it is a design divergence: our base and this PR have both rewritten norm_f32, for different reasons, and the two rewrites are not compatible line-by-line. Ours gained fused multiply/add (template parameters do_multiply/do_add, packed fastdiv dimensions for the mul and add operands, and PDL-aware ggml_cuda_kernel_launch call sites). Theirs changes the kernel signature to take nchannels and nsamples explicitly and wraps the body in two loops so that channel and sample indices beyond the CUDA grid limit are iterated rather than dropped. Merging means keeping our fusion and adding their looping, which requires moving the mul/add pointer arithmetic inside the new loops and threading two more arguments through every launch site -- a real port of the same order as #23685, not an afternoon's work. Deferred rather than guessed at, consistent with how #23685 and #26419 were handled: a patch that compiles and benchmarks fine while being quietly wrong is worse than no patch. SEPARATE AND MORE IMPORTANT FINDING, which applies to the SHIPPED v1 and v2: our base launches norm_f32 with blocks_num(nrows, MIN(nchannels, UINT16_MAX), MIN(nsamples, UINT16_MAX)) but the kernel reads its channel straight from blockIdx.y with no loop, and derives nchannels from gridDim.y -- which is the clamped value. If a NORM ever runs with more than 65535 channels or samples, the excess looks like it is simply not computed, silently. We have never tested that case: the +8 OK ops recorded for this PR earlier were test cases the PR itself adds, so the base was never asked the question. CHEAP EXPERIMENT worth doing when the GPU is free: apply only this PR's tests/test-backend-ops.cpp hunk to the v2 stack, leaving the kernel untouched, and see whether the new large-channel cases fail. If they do, that is a real latent correctness bug in both releases and the port stops being optional. || RESOLVED 2026-09-10, and my suspicion was WRONG. Probe: applied ONLY this PR's tests hunk to the v2 stack, left the kernel exactly as shipped, and ran the NORM family 5 times plus 3 full runs. All seven of the new large-channel cases PASS -- NORM ne=[4,1,65536,1], RMS_NORM ne=[4,1,65536,1] and ne=[4,1,1,65536], L2_NORM, and critically the FUSED variants RMS_NORM_MUL_ADD and both RMS_NORM_MUL_ROPE cases, which are precisely where our base diverges from the PR. So there is no silent truncation beyond 65535 channels in v1 or v2; the frozen base already carries the fix (the tests reference #27901, which is in our base) and the clamped grid I worried about is evidently handled. The hard port is therefore not needed at all, which is a better outcome than doing it. Worth noting the probe nearly fooled me twice: the log read 'files changed: 28' rather than 29, which looked like the test hunk had not applied -- it had, but rel_25206 and rel_28477 already touch that same test file -- and my first filter (-o NORM,RMS_NORM,L2_NORM,GROUP_NORM) silently excluded the fused cases because they carry their own op names.

BLOCKED: the box has CUDA toolkit v11.7 only, while the RTX 5060 Ti is Blackwell (compute 12.0) and needs CUDA 12.8+; the existing bin-cuda came from a prebuilt CUDA 13.3 release, which cannot be rebuilt with the SSD condition toggled. title: Gate pass rule updated: distinguish upstream marginal-tolerance failures from real faults
tg_gain_pct: n/a - harness policy
notes: Measured on this hardware, stock llama.cpp at 73a43d1 fails test-backend-ops in 4 of 20 full runs with no patches applied. A gate that treats any single failing run as a blocker therefore rejects the unpatched upstream code about 20% of the time, which is how the original one-run gate could pass v1 while it carried a real regression -- it was a coin toss either way. THE RULE NOW: (1) never judge correctness from a single run, because init_tensor_uniform seeds from std::random_device and every run uses different input data; (2) always record the ERR = actual > threshold margin, since that is what separates a case sitting on the tolerance line from a genuine fault; (3) compare against the frozen base measured over the SAME number of runs, not against an assumption that the base is clean; (4) a failure is upstream-class if it also occurs on the unpatched base at a comparable rate AND its margin is within a few percent of threshold -- currently the f16 ADD/ADD_ADD family and marginal quantized matvec at n=1. Anything reproducible, absent from the base, or far over tolerance is ours and blocks the release.

title: Finding: where transformer blocks actually do their work, 15 models
tg_gain_pct: n/a - structural study
notes: 2026-09-10. Tudor's redirect: instead of blind layer ablation (28 runs per model, produces a lookup table that transfers to nothing), read the activations as a prompt passes through and get every layer's number from one forward pass. ~3 min of GPU for all 15 models vs an estimated day. Measured per block: turn angle between the residual vector in and out, relative size of the block's contribution, and the attention/FFN split read at the midpoint. Tensors pulled from the compute graph via the eval callback: 'embd' (or 'inp_embd_scaled' on gemma) / 'l_out-<i>' / 'ffn_inp-<i>' or 'sa_out-<i>'. FINDINGS: (1) layer 0 alone carries 11.4% of all turning and takes the embedding from norm ~1 to ~18 -- it builds the representation, never a prune candidate. (2) residual norm rises monotonically in 13/15 models and turn angle falls, which is the mechanism behind deep-layer redundancy. (3) cheap layers cluster at depth 0.5-0.95, cheapest contiguous quarter sits at 0.65-0.87 on average, back third in 11/15. (4) THE SHAPE TRANSFERS ACROSS SIZE CLASSES, NOT JUST WITHIN: pairwise curve correlation excluding layer 0 is 0.57 same-class vs 0.61 cross-class -- the same number, so this is a property of decoder transformers, not of a size class. title: Finding: llama-bench JSON parse silently reported stale numbers

notes: 2026-09-10. Stage 1 of the early-exit question. The earlier prompt-level test found ZERO variation (0 of 444 layers), but it averaged over the tokens inside each prompt, which destroys exactly the variation in question. Re-ran the depth harness emitting one row per (layer, token): 343,759 rows, 4 models, ~2,700 tokens each, 20 wikitext passages. SIGNAL IS REAL: spread of per-token deep-layer effort is 2.1x to 3.0x a shuffled control that breaks the token-to-value link (Qwen3-1.7B 0.638 vs 0.301; Qwen3-4B 0.739 vs 0.268; Llama-3.1-8B 0.767 vs 0.289; gemma-3-4b 0.850 vs 0.280). AND IT IS INTERPRETABLE: the 60 idlest tokens span only 35-54 distinct ids, i.e. they repeat, and decoding them gives ' the', ' a', ' he', ' his' -- function words, exactly what the hypothesis predicts. BUT THE DISTRIBUTION IS SKEWED THE WRONG WAY FOR EARLY EXIT. Median -0.11 to -0.25, p99 up to +3.04, p1 only -0.90 to -1.31: the long tail is tokens needing MORE depth, not a population needing less. At a strict -1 sigma threshold only 0.2-3.9% of tokens qualify, worth ~1% of decode. At a loose -0.5 sigma, 22-27% qualify, worth 8.6-10.5% of decode -- but those tokens are only marginally below average and skipping 40% of the stack for them would be aggressive. SO: ceiling is roughly 10% decode BEFORE paying for the KV-cache hole (a token that exits early leaves no K/V at that position for later tokens to attend to; the standard fix, propagating the exited state upward to compute K/V anyway, hands back much of the saving). Compare with the v2 kernel stack which already delivers +18.6% tg on Llama-3.1-8B with byte-identical output. CAVEAT WORTH RESPECTING: turn angle is a PROXY and it already mispredicted prune safety once (see PRUNE-HYPOTHESIS). title: Finding: 4 patch files were saved as UTF-16 and could never be applied
tg_gain_pct: n/a
notes: 2026-09-10. rel_28616 failed 'git apply' with exit 128 -- a FATAL error, not a context mismatch (which is exit 1) -- and printed no message, even with -v and -3. The source file in the frozen base was byte-identical to what the patch expected, only at a different line offset, so a context conflict made no sense. Cause: the .diff started with FF FE and its bytes read 64 00 69 00 66 00, i.e. UTF-16LE. Windows PowerShell 5.1's Out-File defaults to UTF-16LE, so any patch written with plain Out-File is unreadable by git apply. Scanned the whole patches directory: 4 of 88 affected -- cand_28398.diff (57.6 MB -> 28.5 MB), rel_28613.diff, rel_28616.diff, rel_28671.diff. All four converted to UTF-8 with LF endings; rel_28616 then applies to the base with exit 0. BLAST RADIUS CHECKED, AND IT IS CONTAINED: an earlier 'does not apply' verdict on any of these four would have been an encoding artefact rather than a real conflict, so all four were re-examined. 28613 and 28671 were both dismissed as NOT_APPLICABLE for ARCHITECTURAL reasons -- 28613 adds an RDNA3.5 MMVQ branch our card never takes, 28671 adds a CUB branch our HIP build never compiles -- and both carry applies_clean=n/a, meaning applicability was never the basis of the verdict. Those conclusions stand. cand_28398.diff was misencoded but the v2 stack ships pr28398.diff, a different and correctly-encoded file, and 28398 is VALIDATED on measured speed. So rel_28616 was the ONLY patch this bug actually blocked. PREVENTION: patches must be written with Set-Content -Encoding utf8 or via python, never bare Out-File; and an apply failure with exit 128 should be treated as a malformed patch file, not a conflict.

title: Result: rewriting the prompt to draft ahead is capped near 10% by answer preamble
tg_gain_pct: ceiling ~9% accept, vs 30-40% for plain speculative decoding
notes: 2026-09-11. Tudor's proposal, and it correctly demolished my objection that 'we do not control how users phrase things' -- we control what reaches the model, so an input converter can rewrite the user's text into the high-settling shape while they type, on an otherwise idle GPU. TESTING IT EXPOSED AN ASSUMPTION NO EARLIER EXPERIMENT HAD CHECKED: every score in this line compared the answer from a PARTIAL sentence against the answer from THAT SAME sentence completed -- self-consistency within one phrasing. The converter instead needs the answer to the REWRITTEN prompt to match the answer to the USER'S ORIGINAL, which is a different quantity. MEASURED IT: converting to topic-first shape recovers 27.5% when the user writes question-first, 13.7% when they write first-person declarative, and 0.0% ON ALL TEN when they write conversationally ('have you ever thought about...') -- i.e. it fails completely on exactly the style that motivated the work. CAUSE: the register of the question determines the OPENING of the answer, and prefix matching is made almost entirely of those first characters. Two answers agreeing completely on substance score zero if one opens 'Yes, that is worth considering' and the other 'The main penalty is'. FIX CONFIRMED THE DIAGNOSIS: a register-PRESERVING reorder, keeping the user's own voice and only moving the question last, goes from 0/10 to 7/10 non-zero, mean 9.3%, median 9.6%. So the converter works in principle. VERDICT ANYWAY: ~9% is roughly what drafting from the raw partial text already gives (6-12% on natural prompts), so the converter buys back what a naive rewrite destroys and lands where doing nothing clever lands. THE REAL CEILING IS NOT PHRASING -- it is that this entire metric measures how predictable the answer's PREAMBLE is, not how early the model knows the answer. Classic speculative decoding with a small draft gives 30-40% on every prompt with none of this machinery, so that is the better lever. LAST DOOR NOW TESTED AND SHUT (2026-09-11): suppressing the preamble via a SYSTEM message ('Answer directly. No preamble, no restating the question.') works exactly as diagnosed -- answers change from 'Great question -- and actually, it's a common one! Let's break it down:' to 'Drinking three coffees a day is generally safe for most healthy adults...' -- but it moves cross-phrase accept only 9.3% -> 13.6% mean, with the median flat at ~9.8%, and leaves half-typed self-drafting at ~4%. So preamble is a real effect worth about +4 points, NOT the binding constraint. The ~10% ceiling is genuine: the model's answer is simply not determined until near the end of the question, regardless of phrasing or output format. A third regime using assistant prefill of '- ' scored 19.8%/22.3% with 20/20 non-zero and WAS NEARLY REPORTED AS A BREAKTHROUGH -- it is an artefact. Verification on 3 subjects found the prefill drives the model into repetition loops ('- 1000000000000000000000000000000000000000', '- 100% of the data is lost - 100% of...'), and two identical degenerate strings match each other perfectly. Any regime that raises the score should be checked for degenerate output before being believed. Data results/crossphrase.log, results/regpres.log.

title: Finding: a one-line system message cuts response time 3.8x, dwarfing every kernel gain
tg_gain_pct: -73.6% tokens emitted = 3.8x faster response
notes: 2026-09-11. Came from Tudor's observation that if the model 'thinks less' the output should be faster. THE MECHANISM HE PROPOSED DOES NOT EXIST -- a transformer cannot spend less effort on an easy token, every token is one full pass over all layers and all weights, which PER-TOKEN-DEPTH measured directly (0 of 444 layers ever did less work). BUT THE CONCLUSION WAS RIGHT VIA A DIFFERENT ROUTE: decode cost is per-token, so anything that shortens the answer is a linear speedup. MEASURED, 10 subjects x 4 prompt shapes, Qwen3-4B greedy, max_tokens 1024, cache off. PROMPT SHAPE BARELY MATTERS for length: 696-738 tokens across all four shapes, a 6% spread, so the PROMPT-SHAPE-SEARCH rule does not help here. THE SYSTEM MESSAGE DOES: 'Answer directly. No preamble, no restating the question. Begin with the substance.' takes output from 724.4 to 191.2 tokens, -73.6%, consistent across every shape (-68% to -83%). At 9.2 ms/token on Qwen3-8B that is 6.7 s -> 1.8 s of user-visible latency, a 3.8x speedup from one line of config. NO THINKING BLOCKS INVOLVED: 0 of 40 answers contained <think>, so this is all ordinary answer text. IS IT FREE? MOSTLY, NOT ENTIRELY -- inspected a full pair on the ibuprofen question (561 vs 234 tokens). Both versions carry ALL FIVE medical risks, the 'no legal penalty' clarification and the see-a-doctor advice. The short one loses dosage limits, alternatives and warning signs -- real if secondary content. It sheds 4 markdown headers, 3 horizontal rules, a Recommendations section restating the risks, an emoji Bottom Line and a third repetition of 'talk to your doctor'. Call it 70% ceremony, 30% real content. SO IT IS A TUNABLE VERBOSITY/LATENCY DIAL, NOT A FREE WIN, and a gentler instruction would keep the specifics. PERSPECTIVE WORTH KEEPING: this beats the ENTIRE v2 kernel release (+18.6% decode on Llama-3.1-8B) by roughly a factor of three, costs nothing, took one line, and is completely independent of ROCm, gfx1201 or anything we built -- it works on any model on any backend. notes: Three-line change in ggml_cuda_should_use_mmq(): Q6_K returns true unconditionally on RDNA4 instead of ne11 <= 256. #25940's threshold sends Q6_K to hipBLAS above 256, which on gfx1201 is 2.6x-6.7x SLOWER than MMQ.
